observations: Schema63 retains immutable initialization and update bindings, frozen selections, stable operation IDs, captured instance ownership and snapshot digests. Existing schema62 databases are refused by strict schema checking; no compatibility or downgrade path was introduced.

Initialization mode admits creation and inline history export together before raw context enters the HTTP body. Its export may have happened even when the response is rejected, lost or contains a previously known reference. Receipts show initialization/export admission with no invented confirmed provider reference. A known reused reference is never attached, opened or terminated; history already included in the create request cannot be unexported.

Exact complete provider conversation ACK is required for delivered context. Initialization ACK reads retain the original inline deadline and cannot renew an expired export. Post-creation timing remains explicit and separately tested.

Existing-instance updates use separate retained child receipts with phase/update and original parent delivery ID; the provider reference, native generation, owner, source credentials, endpoint and original listener epochs remain frozen. The bounded queue accepts stable IDs, exact replay returns its original receipt without another export, and root/update operation namespaces cannot collide.

Every actual update and memory use checks initial and all earlier exported selections under one current complete authority interval. A pending unsubmitted selection does not taint prior memory; any exported uncertain, rejected or unacknowledged update blocks subsequent use. Sixteen retained updates per root bound metadata growth and do not discard old-memory authorization.

Assistant registry lock contention yields authority-busy and supplies no read, rather than being misreported as a missing native source. Missing sources remain not-ready and ambiguous sources forbidden; public media already pauses without a current read until its next bounded refresh.

Actual owned SDK audio in both timing modes pauses both directions and clears queued speech while updating. Premature marked provider speech does not reach an independent listener before exact update ACK; actual duplex resumes afterward. Replay creates no new provider call or update. Current authorization loss then stops forwarding, captured cleanup ends the original call and the owned fresh native peer drains.

A terminal update ACK failure records incomplete/uncertain history and confirmed original provider closure without another end command. A lost socket cannot manufacture closure. Late captured observations can record historical custody but do not restore current authority or clear uncertainty.

Recovery processes initialization and child-update metadata without provider IO, reconstructing physical peers, exporting again or adopting provider memory. Child and root rows share one bounded recovery batch. Update lifecycle journal events retain the original resource audience and do not enter model history.

After that actual public/private/return journey, the worker reads the emitted return Session outcome through ApplicationClient and freezes its exact source, journal sequence, actor, body and watermark. All original peers/host drain; a fresh host runtime epoch and signed AI transport retain the same logical Participant. Public context returns the identical historical outcome. One stable follow-up mutation cites that source in past tense, replays without another message, and is attributed to the original AI Participant in independent owner/remote histories. No private transcript is copied or old call claimed live; provider creation/export/end counts remain one.

The actual same-logical-AI runtime combines nine original receipt cases, seven phase failure cases and two fresh owned public duplex modes before the private-only context/duplex/owner-return journey. These are internal profiles of one runtime test, not eighteen extra tests.
